ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a common-emitter NPN transistor switch/amplifier circuit. The emitter is grounded; the base is connected by the input voltage UI through Rb=47 kΩ; the collector is connected to +VCC=+12 V through Rc=1 kΩ; the output voltage UO is taken from the collector with respect to ground, and the right side of the figure marks that the positive terminal of the output terminal is at the collector and the negative terminal is grounded. Then reason: When the transistor is conducting, take UBE=0.7 V, and the input UI=5.4 V, therefore the base current IB=(5.4−0.7)/47 kΩ=4.7 V/47 kΩ=0.1 mA. The current amplification factor β=50, so the collector current IC=βIB=50×0.1 mA=5 mA. The voltage drop on the collector resistor Rc is IC Rc=5 mA×1 kΩ=5 V. The output UO is the collector-to-ground voltage, therefore UO=12 V−5 V=7 V.
